_meta.note: The storm_battery_drain entry copies the wording of Sample 2 (the Part 5 lesson card). The lesson line can be reworded to match your level.
_meta.card_layout: left: two battery curves (what you did vs. alternative). right: three numbered lesson badges.
_meta.note_nasa: Game file. Numbers here are game values, not NASA data.

points.head: The storm blocked the sun.
points.body: Less sunlight means less solar power.

points.head: Power use stayed the same.
points.body: The battery drained faster than planned.

points.head: Lesson: rank before the storm.
points.body: Decide what stays on. Keep a power reserve.

points.head: The sun set.
points.body: Panels make nothing at night.

points.head: The battery was too small.
points.body: It ran out before sunrise.

points.head: Lesson: size the battery for the night.
points.body: Budget for storage, not just panels.

points.head: Four people breathe a lot.
points.body: Oxygen use is steady every sol.

points.head: Plants need power.
points.body: Lights off meant less oxygen made.

points.head: Lesson: protect life support first.
points.body: Cut other loads before air.

points.head: Mars has little air.
points.body: Radiation reaches the ground every day.

points.head: A solar particle event added a spike.
points.body: Sheltering cuts that spike a lot.

points.head: Lesson: spend some budget on shielding.
points.body: Small doses add up over many sols.

points.head: Crew drink every sol.
points.body: Water use never stops.

points.head: Your site had little ice.
points.body: Low-ice sites make less water per sol.

points.head: Lesson: match your site to your needs.
points.body: Ice-rich sites trade sun for water.

points.head: Food stock ran down.
points.body: The crew eats every sol.

points.head: Cutting lights slowed growth.
points.body: Saving power cost food.

points.head: Lesson: every saving has a cost.
points.body: Check what you give up first.

curves.alternative: Heater on at a lower set point

points.head: The heater was off.
points.body: The habitat cooled toward the outside air.

points.head: Mars nights are very cold.
points.body: Temperatures fall far below freezing.

points.head: Lesson: lower the set point, do not switch it off.
points.body: A cooler habitat still saves power.
